arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Smith's counsel argued the substitute expert conveyed out-of-court testimonial statements without personal knowledge.
Arizona's counsel argued the testimony was not offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted.
Justice Alito noted that competent defense counsel could have requested a judgment of acquittal based on evidence.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the limits of expert testimony in criminal trials. It determines whether defendants can cross-examine the actual analyst who performed the testing. The outcome shapes the scope of the Sixth Amendment right to confront witnesses.
